title: Sales are not profit
principle: Sales are not profit. Profit is what's left.

screens.text: Meena sold ₹2 lakh of sarees at the Diwali mela. Her family cheered. Then she counted what was left.

screens.prompt: How much did Meena really make?

options.label: ₹2 lakh, all the money she took in

screens.why: She spent ₹1.9 lakh on sarees, the stall and travel. Only ₹10,000 was left.

screens.title: The rule
screens.text: Sales are all the money that comes in. Profit is what is left after you pay every cost.

screens.title: Meena's sum
screens.text: Sales: ₹2,00,000. Costs for sarees, stall and travel: ₹1,90,000. Profit: ₹2,00,000 − ₹1,90,000 = ₹10,000.

screens.prompt: Next year Meena sells ₹2 lakh again, but her costs fall to ₹1.6 lakh. What is her profit?
screens.why: ₹2,00,000 − ₹1,60,000 = ₹40,000. Same sales, four times the profit.

wrong.b: ₹1.6 lakh is her costs. Take them away from her sales.
wrong.c: Costs come off the sales. You don't add them.

screens.prompt: Money in or money out? Sort Meena's list.

items.text: A buyer pays for a saree
A UPI payment from a buyer

screens.why: Money from buyers is sales. Rent, travel and stock are costs, and they come off before profit.

screens.prompt: Arjun's phone repair shop takes in ₹60,000 this month. Rent, parts and his helper cost ₹45,000. What is his profit?

wrong.a: That adds the costs. Costs come off the sales.
wrong.b: ₹60,000 is his sales. He still has to pay his costs.

screens.text: Sales are the money that comes ___. Profit is what is ___ after every cost.
screens.why: Sales come in. Profit is what stays with you once every cost is paid.

screens.prompt: Asha's stall sold ₹50,000 and kept ₹5,000. Bina's sold ₹30,000 and kept ₹9,000. Who did better?
screens.why: Bina took home ₹9,000. Asha took home ₹5,000. What you keep is what counts.

wrong.a: Asha sold more, but she kept less. Look at what is left.

screens.setup: You make candles at home. Each one costs you ₹19 in wax, wick and jar. A shop wants 1,000 candles at ₹20 each.
screens.question: That is a ₹20,000 order. What do you do?

options.label: Say yes. ₹20,000 is a big order
options.outcome: You work for a month. After wax, wicks and jars, only ₹1,000 is left.
options.why: You looked at the sales, not the profit.
options.better: Take off your costs before you say yes.

options.label: Work out what you would keep first
options.outcome: You see you would keep only ₹1 a candle. You ask the shop for ₹24 a candle instead.
options.why: ₹20,000 of sales is only ₹1,000 of profit. The sum showed you that.

options.label: Say no. Big orders are risky
options.outcome: You lose the order without checking it. A better price could have made it worth it.
options.why: Saying no was safe, but you did not do the sum.
options.better: Do the sum first: sales minus costs.

summary: Sales are all the money that comes in.
Profit is what is left after you pay every cost.

cards.front: A stall sells ₹10,000 in a day and spends ₹9,000. What is its profit?
"We sold a lot, so we made a lot." Is that always true?
cards.back: No. Big sales with big costs can leave nothing.
